entities.name: Siege of Odawara
entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Siege of Odawara, a pivotal event in Japanese history, took place from May 1 to August 4, 1590, in the Odawara Castle. This 93-day conflict saw the combined forces of the Tokugawa and Satsuma clans, led by Tokugawa Ieyasu and Ōtani Yoshitsugu, respectively, besiege and ultimately capture the castle, forcing the Hojo clan into defeat. This decisive victory marked the beginning of the Tokugawa shogunate, which would rule Japan for over 250 years.

The siege was a key moment in the unification of Japan under a single military leader, as Tokugawa Ieyasu's forces defeated the Hojo clan and paved the way for his eventual rise to power. The event also saw the introduction of Western firearms and tactics to Japan, which would have a lasting impact on the country's military history.

The legacy of the Siege of Odawara can be seen in the continued dominance of the Tokugawa shogunate, which ruled Japan until the Meiji Restoration in 1868. The event also had a lasting impact on the city of Odawara, which remains a significant cultural and historical center in Japan to this day. 'The siege was a turning point in Japanese history, marking the beginning of a new era of peace and stability under the Tokugawa regime.'
